text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
WHEAT SALES- South Korea's Cheiljedang Corp and Dongah Flour Mills Co Ltd jointly bought 21,000 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat from Japanese trading house Kanematsu Corp.

- USDA said private exporters reported sales of 110,000 tonnes of HRW wheat to Egypt during 1997/98 marketing year and 110,000 tonnes of hard red winter wheat to unknown destinations for delivery in 1997/98. U.S. exporters also reported purchases from foreign sellers of 110,000 tonnes of HRW wheat to unknown destinations during 1997/98.
WHEAT TENDERS - Sri Lanka seeks 50,000 to 60,000 tonnes of PL-480 wheat for June 30-July 19 shipment. Offers are due by 1630 GMT June 5 at the Sri Lanka embassy in Washington.
BARLEY TENDER - Iran on June 9 will seek 100,000 tonnes of optional feed barley for September shipment, European traders said.
SOYBEAN TENDER - Taiwan's Hui Shung Group will tender Thursday for 46,000 tonnes of soybeans and 8,000 of corn from the United States or South America, traders said.
DURUM TENDER - Algeria on June 3 will seek 150,000 tonnes of optional durum wheat for July and August shipment, European grain traders said.

CORN TENDER - Naseem Agriculture of Abu Dhabi seeks 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes of U.S., Argentine or South African yellow maize for second half August shipment, South Africa's shippers association said. Bids are due June 6.

RICE TENDER - Pakistan's Rice Export Corporation should decide in the next two days on three bids for the export of 5,000 tonnes of basmati variety Pak-7 1996/97 (July-June) rice, containing seven percent broken, an official said.
RICE TENDER - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foostuffs seeks offers June 4 to buy 12,000 tonnes of white rice for July with confirmation on June 12.

MARKET TALK - Cargill Inc said Wednesday it was importing Brazilian soybeans into the United States for use at southeastern U.S. processing plants. The company would not comment on tonnage, shipment dates or prices, but Brazilian traders said they had heard four cargoes had been sold to U.S. firms....The Australian Wheat Board on Wednesday would not confirm or deny a report that Iraq switched an order for 150,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat to Australia.

Reuters quoted U.S. trade sources in Chicago on Tuesday as saying that Iraq was switching the order to 100,000-150,000 tonnes of Australian hard wheat. The switch was probably related to price, the sources said.

... A $4 million barter arrangement between North Korea and U.S. grain giant Cargill Inc was on the brink of falling apart on Wednesday after Pyongyang failed to comply with conditions of the deal, traders said ...Morocco expects its cereal harvest to drop by two-thirds to 3.35 million tonnes in 1996/97 compared with a record 10 million tonnes in 1995/96 season, due to change in the weather, a Moroccan minister said. "Morocco plans to import between 2.4 and 2.5 million tonnes of soft wheat in 1997/98 season, up from 1.1 million tonnes in 1996/97 season," Agriculture Minister Hassan Abou Ayoub said.
